newsitem.title: USA: Clinton picks Lader as U.S. envoy to Britain.
newsitem.headline: Clinton picks Lader as U.S. envoy to Britain.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton announced on Tuesday he would nominate Philip Lader, a long-time friend and former member of his administration, as U.S. ambassador to Britain.
If confirmed by the Senate, Lader would replace Retired Adm. William Crowe.

London would be his first diplomatic post. He completed graduate studies at Oxford University in 1968, has been administrator of the Small Business Administration and was deputy White House chief of staff.
He and his wife Linda in 1981 founded Renaissance Weekends, an annual invitation-only New Years retreat for "innovative leaders" and their families. Clinton and his wife have attended each year.
